raw_response:
I farm the way that keeps my work steady and my risk spread out. I have 10.9 mu, well irrigation, and a wheat-maize system already suited to my land, so I will keep most of the land in that rotation and leave a smaller part for cotton. I will put 8.0 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same 8.0 mu, and I will keep 2.9 mu in cotton. I do that because wheat and maize are the backbone of my farm, irrigation lets me protect yield, and cotton gives me another source of income instead of putting everything into one crop. I have farmed a long time, so I do not chase fancy changes. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps stand and yield, apply enough fertilizer to support irrigated production but not push too hard, irrigate wheat more than maize and cotton because wheat depends more on timely water here, and keep tillage simple with rotary tillage for the grain land and ploughing for cotton so the soil is loose enough for roots. I will control pests with a limited number of sprays and aim for stable yields I believe I can actually manage with my family labor and off-farm work in the household.
